task.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 3b) on REQ-152's test spec and test code.

PASS or FAIL; route to TEST-RUNNER (4) on PASS, back to TEST-DESIGNER on FAIL

checks.skip_tags_or_todos: none found (grep for '@tag :skip' and 'TODO' across both test files and the spec returned no matches)
checks.hardcoded_secrets: none found (grep for password/secret/api_key/token=/connection strings returned no matches)
checks.fixture_isolation: no shared hardcoded state between tests; each test constructs its own Sandbox.new()/Sandbox.new(opts) VM instance
checks.self_sufficiency_and_ordering: verified empirically -- ran combined suite (sandbox_test.exs + platform_test.exs) with three different --seed values (0, 12345, 999) and both file orders; all 57 tests pass identically each time, no ordering dependency
checks.exact_timestamp_test_isolation: platform_test.exs's AC5 describe block sets Application.put_env(:letflow, :lua_platform_time_source, FixedTimeSource) in a `setup` block, captures the PRIOR value via Application.get_env/2 before overwriting, and restores it (or Application.delete_env/2 if none) in `on_exit`. The describe block runs `async: false` at the module level (whole file is async: false) specifically because it mutates process-independent application env that Platform.now/0 reads fresh on every call. config/config.exs:10 sets the production default (Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform.SystemClock) confirming what on_exit restores to in a normal run. The two non-injecting AC4 tests assert only shape/parseability, never a specific value, so they cannot be affected by wall-clock timing. Confirmed genuinely non-wall-clock: the fixed value asserted (~U[2026-01-01 00:00:00.000000Z]) is a hardcoded literal, not derived from the test-run clock.

result.reasoning: All 8 REQ-152 acceptance criteria have runnable, passing test coverage. AC8 is legitimately deferred to TEST-RUNNER per an established spec convention carried over from REQ-151, not a gap. No skip tags, no TODOs, no hardcoded secrets. Tests are self-sufficient and order-independent (empirically verified across 3 seeds / 2 file orders, 57/57 passing each time). The AC5 exact-timestamp test uses a real injected TimeSource behaviour double via Application.put_env, captures and restores the prior value in on_exit, and asserts a hardcoded DateTime literal rather than anything wall-clock-derived -- genuinely deterministic.
